```{r, include=FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

library(maps)
library(leaflet)
library(scales)

block_metrics = readr::read_csv("data/manhattan_block_metrics.csv") %>% 
    mutate(block = as.numeric(block))

block_shapefile = sf::st_read("data/TAX_BLOCK_POLYGON_LAYER/TAX_BLOCK_POLYGON_LAYER.shp") %>% 
    st_transform(crs=4326) %>% 
    filter(BORO == "1") %>% 
    select(BLOCK, geometry) %>% 
    left_join(block_metrics, by=c("BLOCK"="block"))

```

### Manhattan Results

The map below shows block-level metrics for the current co-op sales-based model in Manhattan, 
helping to identify outliers and potential anomalies.

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Define a color palette (from blue to red) using colorNumeric
color_pal_r <- function(x) {
  sapply(x, function(val) {
    if (is.na(val)) return("#999999")  # gray for NA

    if (val >= 1) {
      return("green")  # pure green, consistent with others
    } else if (val >= 0.7 && val < 1) {
      # Green to Yellow: R goes from 0 → 1, G stays at 1
      intensity <- rescale(val, from = c(0.7, 1), to = c(1, 0))  # reverse scale
      return(rgb(intensity, 1, 0))  # green to yellow
    } else if (val >= 0.4 && val < 0.7) {
      # Yellow to Red: G goes from 1 → 0, R stays at 1
      intensity <- rescale(val, from = c(0.4, 0.7), to = c(0, 1))
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))  # yellow to red
    } else {
      return("red")  # solid red for <0.4
    }
  })
}


color_pal_cod <- function(x) {
  sapply(x, function(val) {
    if (is.na(val)) return("#999999")  # gray for NA

    if (val >= 5 & val <= 10) {
      return("green")  # Still using green for the "ideal" zone
    } else if (val < 5) {
      # Values < 5: interpolate from yellow (at 5) to orange (at 0)
      # Yellow = rgb(1, 1, 0), Orange = rgb(1, 0.5, 0)
      intensity <- scales::rescale(val, from = c(0, 5), to = c(0.5, 1))  # Green component goes from 0.5 to 1
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))
    } else {
      # Interpolate from yellow (10) to red (20), capped at red for >20
      capped_val <- min(val, 20)
      intensity <- rescale(capped_val, from = c(10, 20), to = c(1, 0))  # G goes from 1 to 0
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))  # Yellow to Red
    }
  })
}

color_pal_prd <- function(x) {
  sapply(x, function(val) {
    if (is.na(val)) return("#999999")  # gray for NA

    if (val >= 0.98 & val <= 1.03) {
      return("green")  # Ideal range
    } else if (val < 0.98) {
      # Interpolate from yellow (0.98) to red (~0.90)
      capped_val <- max(val, 0.90)  # cap lower bound
      intensity <- rescale(capped_val, from = c(0.90, 0.98), to = c(0, 1))  # G from 0 to 1
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))  # Red to Yellow
    } else {
      # Interpolate from yellow (1.03) to red (~1.10)
      capped_val <- min(val, 1.10)  # cap upper bound
      intensity <- rescale(capped_val, from = c(1.03, 1.10), to = c(1, 0))  # G from 1 to 0
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))  # Yellow to Red
    }
  })
}

color_pal_sales_ratio <- function(x) {
  sapply(x, function(val) {
    if (is.na(val)) return("#999999")  # gray for NA

    if (val >= 0.9 & val <= 1.1) {
      return("green")  # Ideal range
    } else if (val < 0.9) {
      # Fade from yellow (0.9) to red (0.6)
      capped_val <- max(val, 0.6)
      intensity <- rescale(capped_val, from = c(0.6, 0.9), to = c(0, 1))  # G from 0 to 1
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))  # Red to Yellow
    } else {
      # Fade from yellow (1.1) to red (1.4)
      capped_val <- min(val, 1.4)
      intensity <- rescale(capped_val, from = c(1.1, 1.4), to = c(1, 0))  # G from 1 to 0
      return(rgb(1, intensity, 0))  # Yellow to Red
    }
  })
}

color_pal_grosscon <- function(x){
 
  clamped <- pmin(pmax(x, 200000), 5000000)
    
  pal = colorNumeric(
      palette = "Blues",  # You can also use c("#deebf7", "#3182bd") for more control
      domain = c(200000, 5000000),  # fixed scale
      na.color = "#999999"  # gray for NA
  )
  return(pal(clamped))
}
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
leaflet(data = block_shapefile, height=800) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  setView(-73.96, 40.78, zoom = 12) %>%
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>% 
  
  # r layer
  addPolygons(
    group = "By r",
    fillColor = ~color_pal_r(r),
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    color = "white",          
    weight = 1,
    popup = ~paste("Block:", BLOCK, "<br>",
               "n:", n, "<br>",
               "median_sales_ratio:", median_sales_ratio, "<br>",
               "r:", r, "<br>",
               "spearmans:", spearmans, "<br>",
               "cod:", cod, "<br>",
               "prd:", prd, "<br>"
               )
    ) %>% 
  # cod layer
  addPolygons(
    group = "By COD",
    fillColor = ~color_pal_cod(cod), 
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    color = "white",
    weight = 1,
    popup = ~paste("Block:", BLOCK, "<br>",
               "n:", n, "<br>",
               "median_sales_ratio:", median_sales_ratio, "<br>",
               "r:", r, "<br>",
               "spearmans:", spearmans, "<br>",
               "cod:", cod, "<br>",
               "prd:", prd, "<br>"
               )
  ) %>% 
  # prd layer  
  addPolygons(
    group = "By PRD",
    fillColor = ~color_pal_prd(prd), 
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    color = "white",
    weight = 1,
    popup = ~paste("Block:", BLOCK, "<br>",
               "n:", n, "<br>",
               "median_sales_ratio:", median_sales_ratio, "<br>",
               "r:", r, "<br>",
               "spearmans:", spearmans, "<br>",
               "cod:", cod, "<br>",
               "prd:", prd, "<br>"
               )
  ) %>% 
    
  # Add control to switch between the two (overlayGroups with exclusiveGroups)
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("By r", "By COD", "By PRD"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) %>%

  # Only show one group by default
  hideGroup(c("By COD", "By PRD"))
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# get original x/y coordinates
train_df = readr::read_csv("data/train_with_yhat.csv")

train <- sf::st_as_sf(train_df, coords= c("xcoord","ycoord"), crs=2263) %>% 
    st_transform(crs=4326) %>% 
    filter(BORO == "1")
```



This map shows the `r scales::comma(nrow(train))` Manhattan sales in the model, displaying either the sale price or the sales ratio.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Create color palettes

  # Add control to switch between the two (overlayGroups with exclusiveGroups)
```
